prediction.whatIsNeededForEstimate: To put a real number on this claim we need: (1) the unit's square footage, so the $275/sq ft estimate can be converted into an actual dollar figure; (2) the actual price and terms of the 2015 Mostafavi 'bona fide third-party offer' that A&M was required to disclose to Shaw, since that is the baseline cost Shaw would have had to pay to exercise the ROFR and is necessary to compute net appreciation; and (3) a reliable valuation of the unit at the relevant comparison date(s) -- either 2015-16 (when Shaw discovered the breach, relevant to the mitigation/delay defense) and/or present-day/time-of-trial (relevant if the court allows full appreciation through trial), ideally via an appraisal or comparable sale.
prediction.likelyOutcome: The tenant should prevail on liability given A&M's own admission of the breach and the absence of any documented notice, but faces a genuine and fact-supported risk that the court finds waiver/acquiescence bars or substantially limits recovery given the seven-year delay, multiple lease renewals without reservation of the ROFR claim, and Shaw's sophistication as a real estate attorney. Even in a full tenant win, the damages figure cannot be computed from this record because the 2015 Mostafavi offer price and the unit's square footage are both missing.

issues.label: Breach of the Right of First Refusal
Failure to Mitigate / Delay Limiting Damages

outcome.description: After a bench trial the district court awarded the tenant $257,216 in damages plus post-judgment interest, using the tenant's damages methodology (unrealized appreciation, rent-versus-mortgage differential, lost principal) but valuing the unit at the $166.73 per square foot the third-party buyers paid rather than the $275 the tenant proposed. No attorney's fees. The Iowa Court of Appeals affirmed (2-1) on August 19, 2026, rejecting the estoppel-by-acquiescence and failure-to-mitigate defenses.
